hunt.justification: Adversaries are repurposing AI prompt injection techniques for traditional phishing evasion. These invisible characters successfully bypass keyword-based filters; detecting this crossover tradecraft provides high-fidelity signals for active fraud campaigns targeting financial assets.

scenario.summary: A high-volume phishing campaign leveraged invisible Unicode tag characters (ASCII Smuggling) to split financial keywords such as 'funding' in email lures, successfully evading literal keyword filters and NLP-based tokenizers. The campaign utilized over 150 finance-themed domains and followed a strict weekday-only cadence for three months starting in February 2026.

meta.rationale: Targets hosts with Office/M365 installed as primary candidates for email-based phishing interactions. The hunt assumes these hosts are the most likely to be targeted with business-finance lures.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary is using invisible Unicode tag characters to split keywords in finance-themed phishing lures, bypassing traditional email filters and redirecting victims to disposable infrastructure.

encoded_tag_prefix.description: The percent-encoded UTF-8 prefix for characters in the Unicode Tags block.

hunt.name: Unicode-Smuggling Financial Phishing Evasion
hunt.description: This hunt identifies the use of ASCII smuggling characters (U+E0000 to U+E007F) within phishing campaigns targeting financial departments. By inserting invisible TAG characters into lure words like funding, attackers evade literal keyword matching and modern NLP-based classifiers. The hunt uses a gated flow to first identify interactions with campaign-specific domains before performing a deep dive into HTTP headers for percent-encoded smuggling markers and corroborating the activity with network connection patterns that suggest multi-hop redirection.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, package_version FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%microsoft 365%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%office%') GROUP BY device_hostname, package_name, package_version
config.description: Focus the hunt on endpoints running software typically used for processing the phishing lures described in the research.
config.expected_signal: A list of hostnames. Since this is an inventory snapshot, silence means no matching software was found on the monitored fleet.

primitive_config.label: Identify hosts with Office software
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, package_version FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%microsoft 365%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%office%') GROUP BY device_hostname, package_name, package_version
primitive_config.expected: A list of hostnames. Since this is an inventory snapshot, silence means no matching software was found on the monitored fleet.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, query_hostname, COUNT(*) as lookup_count, MIN(time) as first_hit, MAX(time) as last_hit FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{campaign_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0) AND (('{{scope_hosts}}' = '') OR (instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, query_hostname ORDER BY lookup_count DESC
config.description: Identify hosts that have interacted with the known campaign infrastructure as a primary lead.
config.expected_signal: Any hostname resolving the campaign domains is a lead. Silence suggests no direct interaction with the known IOC list occurred via monitored resolvers.

primitive_config.label: DNS hits on campaign domains
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, query_hostname, COUNT(*) as lookup_count, MIN(time) as first_hit, MAX(time) as last_hit FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{campaign_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0) AND (('{{scope_hosts}}' = '') OR (instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, query_hostname ORDER BY lookup_count DESC
primitive_config.expected: Any hostname resolving the campaign domains is a lead. Silence suggests no direct interaction with the known IOC list occurred via monitored resolvers.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, url_hostname, url_full, referrer, user_agent, time FROM hb_http_activity WHERE (LOWER(url_full) LIKE '%' || '{{encoded_tag_prefix}}' || '%' OR LOWER(referrer) LIKE '%' || '{{encoded_tag_prefix}}' || '%') AND (('{{scope_hosts}}' = '') OR (instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify HTTP requests where the URL or referrer contains the specific percent-encoded prefix for Unicode tag characters.
config.expected_signal: A hit identifies the presence of the smuggling block in transit. This is a very rare and high-fidelity indicator of evasion tradecraft.

config.content: SELECT dst_endpoint_hostname, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) as host_count, COUNT(*) as connection_count, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_network_connection WHERE (instr(',' || '{{campaign_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(dst_endpoint_hostname) || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY dst_endpoint_hostname HAVING host_count <= 5 ORDER BY host_count ASC, connection_count DESC
config.description: Evaluate whether connections to the campaign domains are persistent and rare across the fleet.
config.expected_signal: A low host count for a high-volume connection pattern confirms the domains are rare targets rather than legitimate shared infrastructure.

primitive_config.label: Network connection prevalence
primitive_config.content: SELECT dst_endpoint_hostname, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) as host_count, COUNT(*) as connection_count, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_network_connection WHERE (instr(',' || '{{campaign_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(dst_endpoint_hostname) || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY dst_endpoint_hostname HAVING host_count <= 5 ORDER BY host_count ASC, connection_count DESC
primitive_config.expected: A low host count for a high-volume connection pattern confirms the domains are rare targets rather than legitimate shared infrastructure.
